viewing_method: All eight paired sheets viewed at original 1048x1260 resolution, with every source preview at native 512x512; no example omitted

observations.observation: Recognizable fox in both, similar composition; head, body and leg proportions shift. White opaque background remains in both.
Recognizable fox in both; changes to head angle, fur and body outline. Neither preview has a transparent surrounding area.
Blue pixel-art dragon in both. FP8 has a more angular neck/body and a different tail/wing layout; both have a white opaque background.
Visible alpha regression: NF4 has a transparent surrounding area while FP8 has an opaque white background. Horns, outline and pose also change.
Both are large nearly solid black pixel silhouettes with very little floral detail. Transparent surrounding area is present; silhouette shape changes.
Both retain a transparent surrounding area but show a very large solid dark silhouette, with different outlines and little internal flower detail.
Green front-view pixel-art frog in both, with differences in eyes, body and spread limbs. White opaque surrounding background in both.
Both show a standing green frog with transparent surrounding area. FP8 changes eye color, proportions and limb shapes.
Both visibly place the red cube left of a separate blue sphere. Shading, proportions and exact placement differ; no coordinate accuracy is measured.
Left/right relationship is visibly preserved in both. FP8 changes the cube top shading and proportions; this single example is not a statistical spatial validation.
NF4 superimposes the star over the circle. FP8 separates the star above a smaller circle, improving this particular requested relationship.
Both place the star above the circle. The FP8 gap is much smaller, with near contact; perfect separation or exact coordinates are not established.
OPEN is clearly readable in both. FP8 changes the sign scale and the stack of books substantially. Both show several books despite singular wording.
OPEN remains readable. NF4 shows a stack of books; FP8 introduces a wooden shelf of books, a material content change relative to the requested single book.
Both retain a coherent cabin, pines, lake and warm mountain light. Roof, door, chimney and cabin geometry change.
Both retain a coherent cabin beside water and pines. Cabin shape, foliage, shoreline and mountain details shift.

conclusions: Subjects and broad composition are often preserved, with visible changes to details, scale and content.
The dragon at seed 1001 loses the transparent surrounding area in FP8; alpha quality is not uniformly preserved.
The star/circle relationship improves for seed 1000, while other cases show content changes; no perfect-position claim is supported.
On this one paired run FP8 has a lower median generation time and a higher peak allocated VRAM than NF4. This is not a repeated statistical benchmark.
MSE compares output pixels, not ground-truth correctness. No human annotations or human confidence interval were produced.
quality_gate: Comparison evidence only; no universal image-quality or spatial-accuracy pass is asserted
